tldr: In a balanced randomized binary-outcome trial with a growing finite stratum alphabet, this project estimates the entire oracle welfare surface indexed jointly by a monetary budget and a minimum coverage requirement. The surface is represented by a two-price dual whose cell functional is a signed nonsmooth hinge. A shared-pilot arm-symmetric Jackson--factorial construction is asked to achieve expected squared supremum risk of order \(1\wedge d/\{n\log(ed)\}\) without an effect margin or tie restriction, while an anchored full-trial reduction to two-sample \(L_1\) estimation supplies the matching converse on a common open patch where both resource constraints bind. The result is a precision extension to allocation workflows such as \(\texttt{opl\_budget}\), not a claim that existing software reports simultaneous bands.
gap: Published constrained-allocation work characterizes budget-and-coverage threshold policies, and published Qini work gives pointwise regular inference along a one-resource curve. Neither provides a finite-sample minimax theorem for the entire two-resource surface with growing atomic support, unknown masses, exact effect ties, and law-dependent feasibility.
fill: The project derives the bounded dual, resolves the signed cellwise bias and squared-variation certificate, aggregates the process through weighted-halfplane complexity, constructs a total finite estimator, and proves a full-experiment both-active converse at the same rate.
